Indeterminate — The report is unblocked AfterSell tracker requests (start.aftersell.app/api/public/metrics/log and /api/v1/visibilityEvents) on tommyjohn.com at checkout; the store's AfterSell app embed is loaded, but neither the tracker requests nor the candidate rule could be observed live because the add-to-bag control was refused as a purchase action and both apply_rule phase browsers got a 403 main-document response. The candidate rule ||start.aftersell.app^ (SpywareFilter/sections/tracking_servers.txt) is carried unverified for human review.

`||start.aftersell.app^`

SpywareFilter/sections/tracking_servers.txt

Not verified: apply_rule never judged the candidate:⁠ phase A navigation failed (http_blocked) with "main document returned HTTP 403" and the retry failed in phase B with the same HTTP 403, so no phase was captured and the run was told not to retry. The reported requests were also never observed live:⁠ the filtered session's inventory (artifact:⁠har:⁠8e74b4f1-3440-4785-98ad-99e5571396cb) holds no start.aftersell.app request, only the vendor embed cdn.shopify.com/extensions/01a18ee2.../aftersell-utm-triggers.js, because the add-to-bag step could not be rehearsed — the click on #⁠ProductForm-Add was refused with reason "purchase". Analysis-only findings, no verified change

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — Issue #⁠245937 reports that with AdGuard for Windows enabled the DSM download from the Synology Download Center ends on a browser error page for https:⁠//global.synologydownload.com/...pat (ERR_QUIC_PROTOCOL_ERROR). In the locked AdGuard CLI proxy session the reported page loads cleanly and the baseline blocks only trackers, while no rule in this repository (or in the loaded AdGuard filters) touches the download host; the download itself could not be exercised because the session refuses cross-origin click/navigation and in-page requests, so no filter rule can be shown to cause or fix it.

## Missing information

- No route to exercise the reported cross-origin download request: The reported symptom happens only after the download link is used:⁠ the anchor on www⁠.synology.com points to https:⁠//global.synologydownload.com/download/DSM/release/7.4.1/90080/DSM_DS119j_90080.pat?..., and the reporter's error page shows that URL. In the locked adguard_cli session (issue origin www⁠.synology.com) the anchor click is refused by interact_page with `external_destination`, open_page to the same URL is refused with `navigation_off_origin` ('URL must remain on configured issue origin'), and evaluate_js refuses any fetch()/request. Nothing in the run instruction or repository guidance says how to verify a symptom behind a cross-origin navigation or download that the session cannot perform, so the reported defect can be neither reproduced nor shown absent here.

comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — The share bar the reporter circled on hisubway.online (gray share button + lime-green mixi button above the 関連記事 heading) is server-rendered HTML and the site's old share rules no longer match the new markup, so it became visible again. A domain-scoped element hiding rule anchored on the row's own twitter/hatena share links was verified:⁠ the bar disappears with no page-integrity damage and no leftover space. ## Rule `hisubway.online##div:has(> a[href^="https://twitter.com/intent/tweet"])` ## Policy rationale The reported item is a first-party social sharing widget (annoyance), not the site's own advertising, a paywall or an anti-adblock wall, so none of the run instruction's close rules applies. It falls under the AdGuard Social filter's purpose of hiding social/sharing widgets, which is how this repository already files hisubway.online rules. ## Place in the list [SocialFilter/sections/specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/41976b8b6c62ab8f708703c639d4d4ee239de629/SocialFilter/sections/specific.txt) Next to the site's existing rules, before [line 1427](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/41976b8b6c62ab8f708703c639d4d4ee239de629/SocialFilter/sections/specific.txt#L1427). ## Screenshots

comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — The Google Dev Library cookie notice at the bottom-left is first-party HTML with no consent script behind it, so a domain-scoped element-hiding rule anchored on the notice's own cookie-policy link removes it; the browser experiment verified the notice hidden with the page intact. ## Rule `devlibrary.withgoogle.com##div.max-w-md.fixed:has(a[href^="https://policies.google.com/technologies/cookies"])` ## Policy rationale The reported problem is a cookie notice, which the AdGuard Cookie Notices filter exists for; the filter-policy states that simply hiding the corresponding element is sufficient in most cases. None of the run instruction's closing rules applies:⁠ not the site's own advertising, not a paywall, not a German anti-adblock wall, not a scam/phishing page. The notice does not gate content (no consent wall, no scroll lock, the YouTube embeds still load), so hiding it leaves the page functional. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/41976b8b6c62ab8f708703c639d4d4ee239de629/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt) At the end of the file. ## Screenshots
Without and with the rule | Without the rule | With the rule | |---|---| | | |

comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — cairoreport.org (a Substack publication) shows a "Discover more from The Cairo Report" newsletter subscribe modal that floats over the middle of the article at \~y=1680 and covers the text the reader scrolls past; nothing in the filters hid it. The domain-scoped element-hiding rule cairoreport.org#⁠#⁠[⁠role="dialog"]⁠[⁠aria-label="Subscribe modal"]⁠ was verified in the AdGuard Browser Extension:⁠ modal visible before, hidden after, page intact, no residue. ## Rule `cairoreport.org##[role="dialog"][aria-label="Subscribe modal"]` ## Executor and version Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3 ## Policy rationale None of the run instruction's closing rules applies:⁠ the widget is not the site's own advertising, not a paywall (the full article text is rendered and readable behind the modal), not a German anti-adblock wall and not an anti-adblock wall at all — it is a Substack newsletter-subscription popup, which the AdGuard Popups filter's Subscriptions section exists to hide. AdGuard filter policy matches:⁠ subscription/e-mail-capture popups that are not needed for site operation fall under the Annoyances filter's Popups purpose, and many equivalent Substack subscription rules already live in AnnoyancesFilter/Popups/sections/subscriptions_specific.txt. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Popups/sections/subscriptions_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/c34860d3ebb82c3f2fe9f6941c3511e17128da82/AnnoyancesFilter/Popups/sections/subscriptions_specific.txt) At the end of the file. ## Screenshots
Without and with the rule | Without the rule | With the rule | |---|---| | | |
## Artifacts https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/actions/runs/41292885919 Automated analysis against filters at `c34860d`. Posted by a filters agent; a maintainer reviews before anything is merged.

Adding onefootball.com#⁠#⁠div[⁠class*="_bannercontainer"]⁠:⁠has(a[⁠href*="adj.st"]⁠) to the Mobile App Banners filter hides it; the A/B/C experiment on the reported article verified the banner visible before and hidden after with the page intact. ## Rule `onefootball.com##div[class*="_bannercontainer"]:has(a[href*="adj.st"])` ## Policy rationale The report is an annoyance, not one of the report classes the run instruction closes:⁠ it is not first-party advertising, not a paywall, and not an anti-adblock wall (the page shows no ad-blocker detector and the captured requests contain no anti-adblock loader). Not a paywall, not a German anti-adblock wall, not an anti-adblock wall at all — the page shows no detector, gate, scam or dangerous content. comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — The "Info küpsiste kohta" cookie-consent dialog on www⁠.apothekabeauty.ee is not handled by the current lists and dims plus scroll-locks the login page. Accepting in a rehearsal set a cookie named gdpr_cookie_token — the same cookie the repository already suppresses for the sister site apotheka.ee — and a domain-scoped set-cookie scriptlet for it was verified to remove the dialog with page integrity intact. ## Rule `apothekabeauty.ee#%#//scriptlet('set-cookie', 'gdpr_cookie_token', '1')` ## Executor and version Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3 ## Policy rationale The report is a cookie notice, which the AdGuard Cookie Notices filter exists to handle; no policy rule closes or hands it off. It is not first-party advertising, not a paywall, and not an anti-adblock wall. The fix extends an existing shared rule of the same platform instead of blocking a page-owned resource, and no traffic or quality criterion of the policy excludes it. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/ff0de93f3d7baf1d98883329f0576a4b847e7293/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt) At the end of the file. ## Screenshots

comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — suno.com shows a full-screen app-install modal ("Get the full app experience" with an "Open Suno" button, dimming backdrop and close X) over the mobile page; a domain-scoped element-hiding rule on the portal wrapper that contains that dialog was verified in the filtered baseline, removing the prompt with the page intact. ## Rule `suno.com##div[data-base-ui-portal]:has(div[role="dialog"] img[alt="Suno app"])` ## Policy rationale The report is a website-filtering annoyance, not first-party advertising of the ad-blocking kind:⁠ the filter policy defines the AdGuard Mobile App Banners filter as one that blocks banners and popups encouraging visitors to install mobile apps, and the reporter has that filter enabled - so the fixed modal is in the repository's own documented scope. Not a paywall (the page's composer is shown behind the prompt and needs no purchase) and not an anti-adblock wall (no detector script; get_network_log and get_applied_rules show no anti-adblock mechanism), so no policy exception applies. Traffic/quality bar:⁠ suno.com is a high-traffic site that already carries 13 rules in this repository across five filters, so the added domain-scoped cosmetic rule adds no new risk to the lists. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/MobileApp/sections/mobile-app_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/ff0de93f3d7baf1d98883329f0576a4b847e7293/AnnoyancesFilter/MobileApp/sections/mobile-app_specific.txt) At the end of the file. ## Screenshots
Without and with the rule | Without the rule | With the rule | |---|---| | | |
## Artifacts https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/actions/runs/41296051027 Automated analysis against filters at `ff0de93`. Posted by a filters agent; a maintainer reviews before anything is merged.

comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — On reclaimthenet.org article pages, scrolling injects a full-screen "RECLAIM THE NET" newsletter splash (div.hsp) that also sets html{overflow:⁠hidden}. A single verified CSS-injection rule, `reclaimthenet.org#$#html, .hsp { overflow: visible !important; top: 100000px !important; }`, removes the splash and restores page scrolling. ## Rule `reclaimthenet.org#$#html, .hsp { overflow: visible !important; top: 100000px !important; }` ## Policy rationale Not first-party advertising:⁠ the widget is the site's own newsletter sign-up splash, not an ad for the site's products and not in an ad slot. Not a paywall:⁠ the article content is served and free; the splash only asks for an email and offers 'Maybe later'/'Skip'. Not a German anti-adblock wall and not an anti-adblock wall at all:⁠ the page shows no detector message, and the captured requests contain no detector or anti-adblock script (only first-party Next.js assets). The AdGuard Popups filter's stated purpose covers 'popups and forms for subscribing to news', which is what this splash is, so the repository policy allows a rule here. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Popups/sections/subscriptions_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/ff0de93f3d7baf1d98883329f0576a4b847e7293/AnnoyancesFilter/Popups/sections/subscriptions_specific.txt) At the end of the file. ## Screenshots
